text: Security deposit: The security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall be: (a) not exceeding two months' rent, in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceeding six months' rent, in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant on vacating the premises and handing over vacant possession by the tenant to the landlord after making due deductions of any liability of the tenant. Note: Tenancy and rent control laws are State subjects under the Constitution of India; individual State tenancy legislation or rent control acts apply unless the State has enacted legislation adopting this Model Tenancy Act.

Entry into premises: A landlord or the property manager shall not enter the premises let out without giving at least twenty-four hours' notice in writing or by electronic means to the tenant, specifying the day, time, and reason for entry. Such entry shall be between seven in the morning and eight in the evening.

Eviction and recovery of possession: The Rent Court may make an order for eviction and recovery of possession of premises on one or more of the specified grounds: refusal to pay agreed rent; failure to pay arrears of rent within one month of notice; sub-letting whole or part without written consent; misuse of premises causing nuisance or structural damage. Landlords cannot evict tenants or cut essential services (water, electricity) without due process before the Rent Court.

Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts: Save as otherwise provided in this Act, no civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of the provisions to which this Act applies regarding regulation of rent, eviction, or recovery of possession of tenancy premises, which are triable by the Rent Authority and Rent Court.
